input.summary:
P0 west bedroom module (parts/room-6.mjs) is written: two beds at z17-18 with heads on the west wall, barrel dressers at both ends, lamp post and lanterns. On a scratch copy the room check says OK (walk 14/14, min light 12, FIT OK) and the render reads correctly.
In the real make.sh build the furniture is REFUSED (15 writes, 0 placed) because shell-west fills every interior cell with air, and runParts locks that air. The fix belongs in shell-west (or runParts), not in this part.
The bedroom's east partition (x5) is not built by any part yet, so the upper hall is open to the room; I logged the lock blocker in plan.md Notes.
left: BLOCKED: shell-west's house() writes air into every interior cell (g.fill(..., "air")); runParts locks placed air, so all P0 west bedroom furniture is refused in make.sh (15 refused, 0 placed). Needs shell-west to leave interior cells unset (or runParts to treat air as unplaced); then re-run ./make.sh and the room check on build.nbt.

The partition wall x5 between the west bedroom and the P0 upper hall (z14..20, door at z16) is not built by any part; the bedroom is open to the hall in the current build. Heads are placed on the west wall (x2) so the beds do not depend on it, but the room needs the wall.

parts/room-6.mjs uses a local placeBed() instead of the library bed(), because bed() treats the namespaced air id "minecraft:air" (as returned by a loaded grid) as not air and refuses every bed. Library fix: accept air by /air$/ in bed()'s free test.
Verified on a scratch copy only (/tmp/room6-check: load build.nbt, run build(g), save): room check OK, render looks right. The real build.nbt does not contain this room's furniture yet.

waste.what: Checking my room's furniture: I had to write a scratch loader to run the room module on the built structure, because runParts refuses the writes and the room check on build.nbt showed the room empty.
waste.tool: A `mcd room --part <module>` (or `--scratch`) mode that runs one part's build on a copy of the built structure without the runParts lock, and reports what it would refuse, so a designer sees the lock conflict up front.

waste.what: Two beds placed by a local placeBed() because the library bed() rejects the namespaced air id "minecraft:air" on a loaded grid.
waste.cost: one failed check, one rewrite of the helper
waste.tool: Fix bed() in tools/src/build.mjs to treat any id ending in air (including minecraft:air) as free, so designers can call bed() on a loaded grid.

waste.what: Working out the 2x7 room's walkable lanes, bed rows and window/wall cells by hand from the plan grid, which showed doorway marks (D) where the unbuilt partition is only air.
waste.cost: roughly 3 layout iterations (beds first at z19-20, then z17-18 once the partition showed as open)
waste.tool: `mcd plan` should mark a wall cell as unbuilt rather than as a doorway when the shell has not built it, and report which room walls are missing.

companions.task: Leave the interior cells of each house unset instead of filling them with air, so the room designers can place furniture; build the x5 partition walls between the bedrooms and the halls with the door at z16 cut.
A second pair of hands to check bed heads against solid walls and to lay the barrel dressers; a bed joiner who knows bed() on a loaded grid.
Confirm the light map on the built copy (min 12 on the scratch copy) once the furniture is in the real build.
